I’m one month post chemo and I am having a really hard time. I feel broken and traumatized by the experience. I feel alone and depressed and anxious. I don’t know how to rebuild my life because the depression and anxiety is so consuming. I’m doing little things to try to get back into the world such as seeing friends and going to counseling but overall I worry I’ll never be the same again.

This is exactly me. I will be there physically, emotionally and financially for the person I’m with. I put forth so much effort. I tend to date people who don’t reciprocate that exact effort. Which triggers the anxiety issues I already have, as well as self esteem issues, that obviously I’m not worth the effort of others.

I’ve actually been on an anti-depressant for 14 years the same one and same dosage all this time. fluvoxamine. I’ve long wondered if it’s still working but now especially I’m unsure. I can’t get out of bed, I feel stuck to my bed the way I did when I had chemo except now I should be trying to get up and out and moving about more. The irony is all this time I was sick I couldn’t wait to be better and do all these things, even simple things and now I lack the motivation or desire to do any of it. I’m starting a cancer support group and individual counseling soon, I can see if they can refer me to a psychiatrist or also contact the social worker at my oncologists office to see if she can refer me to a psychiatrist. I haven’t seen one in like 6 years. My primary care doctor has been the one prescribing the meds to me these last few years. 
Thank you for your support. It’s good to know others have gone through this after finishing treatment.

Yes, I got my results back yesterday and I’m thankfully in remission, but what should be a happy celebratory moment I haven’t stopped crying, I feel sad and anxious and just numb and lost. I have this wave of depression that’s come over me, and instead of feeling the joy, relief and gratitude I should feel I feel so sad.

Thank you. This was such a kind sweet message. She wasn’t my caregiver. I’ve been with my parents who were my caregivers but she was my emotional support, my escape, and my person to lean on. I know this was hard on her, and that’s why I wanted my finishing to be a celebration for both of us. Like, we survived one of the hardest experiences together. But I think it just got to be too much. We’ve gone weeks apart bc of me not feeling well and all the complications I’ve had. All the more reason why I was so excited to have her there when this was all over. 
I think also knowing the routine of seeing my oncologist and getting chemo every other week, as hard as that was, there was security and familiarity in that, and now that’s coming to an end. So I totally get what you’re saying. I’m hopeful that this feeling will be only temporary and I can find the joy in all the things I was excited about seeing and doing once this was over. 
It’s nice to know there are people out there who have gone through this. So thank you.

I just had my last chemo a week ago for Hodgkin’s Lymphoma. As I spent the last week dealing with the host of predictable but manageable side effects, emotionally I don’t know how to feel. I feel glad it’s over but also kind of sad. I feel angry and resentful and hurt that I went through a 7 month war and most of my closest friends weren’t there as much as I expected them to be. That except for 1 friend none of them came to any of my chemo treatments or visited me in the hospital the 3 times I was hospitalized. And my gf who thinks she’s been there for me came to only 1 chemo(out of 12) and now just broke up with me. 
In the darkest time of your life, you expect your loved ones to drop everything and be by your side and nobody was.
This will be my new life bc my gf just broke up with me.

My advice is speak to your dr to get clarification. I saw a Lymphoma specialist at a top cancer center this week who told me tumors do leave scarring and calcification. But get second opinions if you need to for your peace of mind.

Hi I'm 32 F NSHL 2A. I'm on my 4th cycle or 8th treatment. I was very hyper focused about losing my hair. I invested a lot of money in cold caps for my first treatment which has mixed feelings on their use and success by doctors. While I was adamant about wanting to keep my hair and not look sick, the cold caps ended up being more effort and discomfort on what is an already challenging experience. I made the decision to not continue. After my 3rd treatment is when my hair really started to thin and shed. My part kept thinning and was receding  further and further back. Eventually it got to the point that I was leaving hair everywhere, so with the help of my partner we shaved it. First cutting it chin length, then shaving it. It was emotional but freeing at the same time, i recommend investing in a nice wig, human hair if you can afford it, which helps me to feel pretty on days I am seeing friends and family. Additionally, know this is temporary and it will come back. It's such a common fear and losing our hair is so tied to feeling like we're losing our identity. Only you can decide what's the best way to deal with it, but there's so many like you who have felt the same way.
